feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: IPAC'26 talk (M. Convery, 19 May 2026), slide "Accelerator program evolution"
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Planned, not yet in operation. Schedule bounds from the same talk: after the 2028-2029 "long shutdown" the Booster is commissioned with PIP-II beam, and "Operation of LBNF beam to DUNE will begin in 2031". The talk's draft schedule is as of May 2026.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: Booster commissioning with beam from the PIP-II linac uses the Booster Neutrino Beam facility which allows an experimental program if approved

start.display: after the 2028-2029 long shutdown; LBNF beam to DUNE planned for 2031

intervals.label: development and construction
intervals.note: The 2017 status paper calls PIP-II "under development"; pip2.fnal.gov and lbnf-dune.fnal.gov describe it in the present tense as being built. Neither a groundbreaking date nor a completion date could be sourced from a fetchable page.

beam_energy.quote: replacement of the existing 40-years old 400 MeV normal-conducting Linac with a modern 800 MeV superconducting RF linear accelerator

beam_power.note: Beam power delivered on the LBNF target by the Main Injector once PIP-II is running, not the linac beam power.
beam_power.quote: It aims at 1.2MW beam power on target at the start of the LBNF/DUNE experiment

length.quote: The heart of PIP-II is a 215-meter-long particle accelerator, featuring major contributions from international partners and the latest superconducting radio-frequency technology developed at Fermilab.

summary.plain: A new 215-metre superconducting accelerator being built at Fermilab. It will replace the old first-stage machine and let the laboratory make the most intense high-energy neutrino beam in the world.
summary.technical: 800 MeV CW-capable superconducting RF H- linac replacing the 400 MeV normal-conducting linac, injecting into the Booster and enabling 1.2 MW of 60-120 GeV protons on the LBNF target.
